service: API Portal discovers the APIs running in your AWS accounts and organization, lets you manage them as Managed APIs, and publishes their documentation to developer portals.

operations.AssociateManagedApis: Associate one or more Managed APIs with a product. Best-effort — IDs that fail are returned in {@link AssociateManagedApisResponse#failedItems}; IDs that succeed are omitted. Associating an already-associated Managed API is a no-op (not reported as failure).
operations.CreateManagedApi: Promote a discovered API in the API inventory into the managed API list.
operations.CreatePortal: Creates a portal that publishes documentation for the products it includes. Use UpdatePortalPublishStatus to publish it.
operations.CreatePortalPreview: Starts building a preview of the portal's current content. Use GetPortal to check the preview status and get the preview URL.
operations.CreateProduct: Creates a product. A product groups Managed APIs with their API pages and product pages so a portal can publish them together.
operations.CreateProductApiPage: Creates an API page that documents a Managed API in a product. The page content is generated asynchronously. Use status to track it.
operations.CreateProductPage: Creates a product page with free-form documentation. A product can have up to 40 pages.
operations.DeleteDiscoveryConfiguration: Deletes the discovery configuration and stops any running discovery.
operations.DeleteOrganizationDiscoveryConfiguration: Deletes the organization-wide discovery configuration and stops any running discovery across the organization. Only the organization management account may call this operation.
operations.DeleteProductSharingPolicy: Deletes the sharing policy of a product. The product is no longer shared.
operations.DisassociateManagedApis: Disassociate one or more Managed APIs from a product. Best-effort — IDs that fail are returned in {@link DisassociateManagedApisResponse#failedItems}; IDs that succeed are omitted. Disassociating an unmapped Managed API is a no-op (not reported as failure).
operations.GetApiInventoryItem: Gets full details of a single API inventory item.
operations.GetDiscoveryConfiguration: Retrieves the discovery configuration for the account and region.
operations.GetManagedApi: Returns a Managed API, including its security posture findings.
operations.GetOrganizationDiscoveryConfiguration: Retrieves the organization-wide discovery configuration. Only the organization management account and registered delegated administrators may call this operation.
operations.GetPortal: Returns the configuration, publish status, and preview status of a portal.
operations.GetProduct: Returns a product. To read a product shared with you by another account, supply resourceOwnerAccountId.
operations.GetProductApiPage: Returns an API page, including its body.
operations.GetProductPage: Returns a product page, including its body.
operations.GetProductSharingPolicy: Returns the sharing policy of a product.
operations.ListApiInventoryItems: Lists discovered API inventory items with filtering and pagination.
operations.ListManagedApiEvents: Lists API-security events for a single managed API, most recent first. Returns up to 20 of the most recent events (not paginated).
operations.ListManagedApis: Lists the Managed APIs in your account.
operations.ListProductApiPages: Lists the API pages in a product. The results do not include page bodies.
operations.ListProductPages: Lists the product pages in a product. The results do not include page bodies.
operations.ListProducts: Lists products you own, products shared with you, or both.
operations.ListTagsForResource: Lists the tags for an API Portal resource. One of the three basic tagging operations generated for Tagris integration (ListTagsForResource / TagResource / UntagResource).
operations.PutOrganizationDiscoveryConfiguration: Creates or updates the organization-wide discovery configuration. This is a singleton per organization. Only the organization management account and registered delegated administrators may call this operation.
operations.PutProductSharingPolicy: Creates or replaces the sharing policy of a product. The policy controls which other accounts can read the product.
operations.TagResource: Adds or updates tags on an API Portal resource. One of the three basic tagging operations generated for Tagris integration (ListTagsForResource / TagResource / UntagResource).
operations.UntagResource:
Removes tags from an API Portal resource. One of the three basic tagging operations generated for Tagris integration (ListTagsForResource / TagResource / UntagResource).

tagKeys is a query string parameter: for tag-based access control (TBAC/ABAC) to work correctly, API Gateway requires the keys to be removed to be passed as a query string parameter.
operations.UpdatePortal: Updates a portal. Only the fields supplied in the request are changed.
operations.UpdatePortalPublishStatus: Publishes or disables a portal. The change runs asynchronously. Use GetPortal to track publishStatus.
operations.UpdateProduct: Updates a product. Only the fields supplied in the request are changed.
operations.UpdateProductApiPage: Updates an API page. Only the fields supplied in the request are changed.

ApiSelectionMode.base:
How a product's member Managed APIs are chosen. CUSTOM - the customer associates and disassociates Managed APIs explicitly. RULE_BASED - membership is derived from ruleFilters: every Managed API in the account that matches is associated, and nothing else is. BatchAssociateManagedApi and BatchDisassociateManagedApi are rejected for these products.

Fixed at create time. UpdateProduct cannot change the mode of an existing product.

Classification.base:
Whether any account has created a ManagedApi for a discovered API, and for a managed API whether it is unused or no longer in the caller's organization. SHADOW - no account has created a ManagedApi for this item. MANAGED - some account in the caller's organization has created a ManagedApi for this item. MANAGED_ZOMBIE - managed and unused: no traffic for at least the account's no-traffic window. The API is still reachable, so this clears once traffic resumes. MANAGED_ORPHANED - managed, but the account hosting the API has left the caller's organization or been closed. The item is a last-known snapshot: it is no longer rediscovered, and its findings are not authorized for the caller. An organizational unit move is not a trigger.

MANAGED_ZOMBIE and MANAGED_ORPHANED add detail to a MANAGED item, so neither is returned for an item the caller does not manage, and MANAGED_ORPHANED takes priority over MANAGED_ZOMBIE. Both are derived per request rather than stored, so neither expires on its own.

Host.base: A discovered API's front-door hostname (e.g. an ALB, CloudFront, or API Gateway DNS name), bounded by the DNS name limit (RFC 1035). Usually literal, but may contain placeholders: <> - stands for one dot-separated part of the hostname. When 10 or more hosts differ only in that part, they fold into one, e.g. a.example.com, b.example.com, ... become "<>.example.com". Deeper levels fold the same way ("<>.<>.example.com"). The registrable domain never folds. - an IP-literal host.

refs.CreatePortalResponse$rumAppMonitorName: The name of the CloudWatch RUM app monitor that collects reader telemetry for the portal.

refs.UpdatePortalResponse$rumAppMonitorName: The name of the CloudWatch RUM app monitor that collects reader telemetry for the portal.

refs.ApiInventoryFilters$resourceArn: Return only APIs served by this resource.
refs.ApiInventoryItem$resourceArn: The ARN of the resource that serves the API, such as an API Gateway stage or a load balancer.
refs.ApiInventoryItemDetail$resourceArn: The ARN of the resource that serves the API, such as an API Gateway stage or a load balancer.
refs.ApiSignature$resourceArn: The ARN of the resource that serves the API.
refs.GetApiInventoryItemRequest$resourceArn: The ARN of the resource that serves the API, such as an API Gateway stage or a load balancer.
refs.IdentifierParts$resourceArn: The ARN of the resource that serves the API.

refs.DiscoveryConfigurationData$excludedResou: The ARNs of resources left out of discovery.
refs.DiscoveryExclusionFilters$resourceArns: List of resource ARNs to exclude. Only ELB and CloudFront resource ARNs are supported.
refs.PutDiscoveryConfigurationRequest$exclude: The ARNs of resources to leave out of discovery, up to 50.

ResourceNotFoundException.base: The requested resource does not exist, or you do not have access to it.

refs.ListProductsRequest$resourceOwner: Whose products to return: SELF for your own, OTHER_ACCOUNTS for products shared with you, or ALL. Defaults to ALL, or to SELF when managedApiId is supplied.

RuleFilter.base: Values are compared to the attribute as literals: exact and case-sensitive, no wildcards.

RuleFilterKey.base: The Managed API attribute a RuleFilter compares against. RESOURCE_ARN - apiSignature.resourceArn HOST - apiSignature.hostname METHOD - apiSignature.method, so values must be HttpMethod names PATH - apiSignature.path PORT - apiSignature.port, compared as its decimal string, so values must be 0-65535 with no leading zeros ACCOUNT - the account hosting the API, which for an ORGANIZATION-scoped Managed API is the member account rather than the account that created it

RuleFilterList.base: One filter per RuleFilterKey: filters are AND-ed, so two on the same key never both match.

refs.ApiSelectionConfiguration$ruleFilters: Required for RULE_BASED, rejected for CUSTOM. Filters are combined with AND, the values within one filter with OR, and evaluated only over the account's Managed APIs. Replaced as a whole on update, not merged.

RuleFilterValue.base:
Bounded by the longest matchable attribute, apiSignature.path.

No whitespace: none of the matchable attributes (ARN, hostname, method, path, port, account) contain any. Per-key formats (METHOD, PORT, ACCOUNT) are enforced in ProductValidator.validateRuleFilterValue, since one pattern cannot express them for a value shared by every key.

refs.RuleFilter$values: The values to match. The filter matches when the attribute equals any of them.

Section.base: A named group of API pages in the portal navigation.

refs.Section$sectionName: Shown in the portal navigation. Same bound as page titles and operation names, and no control characters (the service rejects a blank name).

refs.CreateProductApiPageResponse$status: The status of the page content: IN_PROGRESS while it is generated, then AVAILABLE or FAILED.
refs.GetProductApiPageResponse$status: The status of the page content: IN_PROGRESS while it is generated, then AVAILABLE or FAILED.
refs.ProductApiPageSummaryNoBody$status: The status of the page content: IN_PROGRESS while it is generated, then AVAILABLE or FAILED.
refs.UpdateProductApiPageResponse$status: The status of the page content: IN_PROGRESS while it is generated, then AVAILABLE or FAILED.

refs.ApiInventoryItem$region: The AWS Region the API was discovered in.
refs.ApiInventoryItemDetail$region: The AWS Region the API was discovered in.
refs.GetProductApiPageResponse$rawDisplayCont: The Markdown body of the page. Returned only when includeRawDisplayContent is true.
refs.Preview$previewUrl: The URL to view the preview. Present when previewStatus is PREVIEW_READY.

refs.StartDiscoveryRequest$id: Identifier of the discovery configuration to start. Required. Today this is the configuration ARN, which carries the owner account id so a delegated admin or org admin can start an org-scoped configuration that lives in a different account.
refs.StopDiscoveryRequest$id: Identifier of the discovery configuration to stop. Required. Today this is the configuration ARN, which carries the owner account id so a delegated admin or org admin can stop an org-scoped configuration that lives in a different account.

TagKey.base: A tag key of 1-128 Unicode characters, per the AWS tagging limits.

refs.UntagResourceRequest$tagKeys: The keys of the tags to remove, up to 50.

TagValue.base: A tag value of 0-256 Unicode characters, per the AWS tagging limits; an empty value is valid.

Tags.base: Up to 50 tags per request, matching API Gateway's limit of 50 tags per resource.

ThreatCategory.base: OWASP API Security category, e.g. "API2:2023". Open string — OWASP revises the list per edition.

ThreatLabel.base: Detection label describing the attack and its confidence tier, e.g. "awswaf:managed:aws:api-security:credential-stuffing-high".

refs.ApiInventoryItem$lastSeen: When discovery most recently observed the API.
refs.ListManagedApiEventsRequest$startedAfter: Inclusive lower bound on each event's start time; only events that started at or after this time are returned. Optional; defaults to 30 days before the current time.
refs.ListManagedApiEventsRequest$startedBefor: Exclusive upper bound on each event's start time; only events that started before this time are returned. Optional; defaults to the current time.
refs.ManagedApiEventSummary$endedAt: When the event completed; absent while it is still in progress.
refs.PortalTheme$logoUploadedAt: When the portal logo was last uploaded. Absent if the portal has no logo.

refs.CreateProductApiPageRequest$tryItState: Whether readers can call the API from the page with Try-It. Defaults to DISABLED. To enable it, the page's API URL must use HTTPS on a domain that supports Try-It.
refs.CreateProductApiPageResponse$tryItState: Whether Try-It is enabled on the page.
refs.GetProductApiPageResponse$tryItState: Whether Try-It is enabled on the page.
refs.ProductApiPageSummaryNoBody$tryItState: Whether Try-It is enabled on the page.
refs.UpdateProductApiPageRequest$tryItState: The new Try-It setting. Omit it to keep the current setting. To enable it, the page's API URL must use HTTPS on a domain that supports Try-It.
refs.UpdateProductApiPageResponse$tryItState: Whether Try-It is enabled on the page.

refs.CognitoConfig$userPoolArn: The ARN of the Cognito user pool.

refs.CognitoConfig$userPoolDomain: The domain of the user pool's hosted sign-in pages.

Visibility.base: Whether a discovered API is reachable publicly or only from within a private network.

WafApiSecurityEventDetail.base: Detail specific to a WAF API-security event.

refs.ManagedApiEventSummary$wafApiSecurityEve: Detail specific to a WAF API-security event; populated when eventType is WAF_API_SECURITY.

WafStatus.base: Whether a WAF web ACL is attached to the API's front-door service.

WebAclArn.base: ARN of the WebACL that produced the event. Carried on the event detail so GetManagedApiEvent can fetch the event's full detail; scope and region are derived from it.

Workload.base: An AI protocol seen in an API's traffic, detected by the front door from request or response headers (and, for A2A, a query parameter). MCP - Model Context Protocol. LLM - traffic to or from an LLM inference server or gateway. A2A - Agent2Agent protocol.

refs.ApiInventoryItem$workloads: AI protocols seen in this API's traffic, each listed at most once. Absent when none has been reported, which includes an account that has not enabled AI discovery.
refs.ApiInventoryItemDetail$workloads: AI protocols seen in this API's traffic, each listed at most once. Absent when none has been reported, which includes an account that has not enabled AI discovery.
